theorem difference_mod_four (p h k : Int) (s : Nat) :
    4 ∣ shell p (p+1+4*h) k (s+1) - shell p (p+1+4*h) k s - p^s*(p-k) := by

evidence: shell matches b_0=1, b_1=a-k, b_{s+2}=a b_{s+1}-p b_s; divided_shell with p=2t+1, a=p+1+4h, k=2z+1 gives 2|d and d/2 = (a-k-1)/2 mod 2 for all s, which is (O.10) with kappa=k. It needs only odd p and odd k, where [M] has a prime p with kappa in {1,-1}; no extra hypothesis was overlooked.

HeckeShell.shell is exactly [M]'s recurrence (b_0=1, b_1=a-k, b_{s+2}=a b_{s+1}-p b_s), and divided_shell proves, with no further hypotheses, that b_{s+1}-b_s is even and (b_{s+1}-b_s)/2 = (a-k-1)/2 mod 2 for all s, for any odd integer p=2t+1, any a=p+1+4h and any odd k=2z+1; [M] needs p a prime and kappa in {1,-1} (p not dividing D), so the Lean statement is a strict, if mild, generalization and I found no overlooked hypothesis (the divisions are exact since both numerators are even, so Int ediv/emod agree with [M]'s congruence).
